=== DOCS-VERIFICATION (trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html) ===
• Verbatim docs rule: "When a GROUP BY clause is used in a SELECT statement all output expressions must be either aggregate functions or columns present in the GROUP BY clause." Applies to ORDER BY in a GROUP BY query because ORDER BY operates on rows produced AFTER GROUP BY — so its expressions must resolve to GROUPING expressions, AGGREGATE functions, or SELECT-list output aliases / ordinal numbers.
• Verbatim docs rule (ORDER BY): "each expression may be composed of output columns, or it may be an ordinal number selecting an output column by position, starting at one."
• Confirmed via WebSearch — the error 'must be an aggregate expression or appear in GROUP BY clause' is raised by Trino's analyzer when ORDER BY references a raw ungrouped column. The function-wrapping (e.g. day_of_week(...) wrapping order_date) does NOT make it legal — analyzer looks through the wrapping function to the bare column.

=== THREE VALID OPTIONS (all docs-verified, valid Trino 467, no :: cast) ===
• OPTION A (group-by-the-number): GROUP BY day_of_week(order_date) (returns ISO 1=Mon..7=Sun) + project name via CASE day_of_week WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday'...WHEN 7 THEN 'Sunday' END + ORDER BY day_of_week(order_date) — legal because the sort key IS a grouping expression.
• OPTION B (aggregate-wrap-min): keep GROUP BY format_datetime(CAST(order_date AS timestamp), 'EEEE') + ORDER BY min(day_of_week(order_date)) — min() makes it an aggregate (every row in a weekday group ties on day_of_week, so min returns that number).
• OPTION C (ordinal): SELECT day_of_week(order_date) AS dow, CASE...END AS day_name, SUM(amount) AS revenue ... GROUP BY day_of_week(order_date) ORDER BY 1 — ordinal 1 references output column position 1 (always valid).

=== DO-NOT-WRITE (the EXACT iter660 Q2 bug) ===
• SELECT format_datetime(CAST(order_date AS timestamp), 'EEEE') AS day_name, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY format_datetime(CAST(order_date AS timestamp), 'EEEE') ORDER BY day_of_week(order_date)
• WHY: order_date is NOT in GROUP BY (only format_datetime(order_date,...) is) and NOT aggregated. Trino: 'order_date must be an aggregate expression or appear in GROUP BY clause'.
• FIX: GROUP BY day_of_week(order_date) too, OR ORDER BY min(day_of_week(order_date)), OR ORDER BY 1.
